title: Google Antigravity /teamwork & DuoDiscover Accelerate TPU Kernels 4.09×, Cut Borg Preemptions & Port libgav1
aiSystem: Google Antigravity /teamwork & DuoDiscover (Gemini 4 Argon Multi-Agent Harness)
whyItMatters: Antigravity /teamwork’s DuoDiscover sped up JAXBench TPU kernels 4.09× and vLLM Pallas kernels 2.99×, shipped Borg patches cutting TPU preemption 24%, and ported libgav1 to 20–30% faster Rust.
summary: Published by Google Research and Google DeepMind on November 13, 2026 alongside its Weil Conjectures and Courtade–Kumar math breakthroughs, the Antigravity /teamwork multi-agent harness (running on Gemini 4 Argon) demonstrated autonomous long-horizon systems-engineering breakthroughs across production ML compilers, fleet scheduling, and safety-critical C++ migration. Solving the hardware-evaluation bottleneck via DuoDiscover—where parallel agents jointly discover code bottlenecks and synthesize 23-second proxy 'yardstick' evaluators continuously calibrated against full 7–32 minute TPU runs via Kendall rank correlation—the system achieved a 4.09× geometric-mean speedup across 17 JAXBench kernels and a 2.99× speedup across 7 hand-optimized vLLM TPU-Inference Pallas kernels. Simultaneously, /teamwork shipped two production Borg scheduler optimizations cutting TPU workload preemption by 24%, identified >1 pebibyte of fleet memory savings, and ported Google’s ~170K-line libgav1 AV1 video decoder to memory-safe Rust running 20–30% faster than C++ (alongside an ~800K-line Zircon microkernel port).
technicalHighlights: DuoDiscover agents invented fast 23-second proxy 'yardsticks' validated by Kendall rank correlation against 7–32 minute hardware runs, delivering 4.09× geometric-mean speedup on 17 JAXBench kernels and 2.99× on 7 hand-optimized vLLM TPU Pallas kernels.
Shipped two production Google Borg scheduler changes reducing TPU workload preemption by 24% while preserving SLOs and fleet utilization, plus >1 PiB fleet memory savings.
Autonomously rewrote Google’s libgav1 AV1 video decoder (~170K lines) into memory-safe Rust that beat the original C++ performance by 20–30% after profiling-guided optimization.
caveats: Reported via Google Research technical blog rather than a peer-reviewed conference paper; independent third-party reproduction of production Borg fleet metrics and full Zircon microkernel completeness has not yet been externally audited.

scoreRationale.foundational: Introduced DuoDiscover’s co-evolution of code optimizations and rank-calibrated proxy evaluators, solving the evaluation-latency bottleneck of autonomous systems engineering.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly transforms production ML compiler/kernel optimization, hyperscale datacenter scheduling, and large-scale C++-to-Rust memory-safety migration.
scoreRationale.verification: Backed by shipped production Google Borg fleet changes and hardware-measured TPU/AV1 benchmarks, though awaiting peer-reviewed publication and external code audits.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed weeks of expert kernel tuning and multi-year systems rewrites into autonomous multi-agent campaigns.
